description:
LANDED c2c723c63 on wt/kdt-close (PR #110, draft), 2026-09-03. The last ticket
of the arc's confluence chain, and by the time it was built it was a PURE
DELETION.

WHAT THE CLEANER WAS, AND WHY ITS REASONING WAS WRONG:
drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings (fz-f98.16) removed every variable binding
a position collected through an exact `[]` witness, on the reasoning that "[]
is a member of every list type, so a binding it pins is noise". That is false
about this code: collect_instantiation_subst([a], []) binds NOTHING, because
the element of `[]` is none and none-bindings are never collected. So the
cleaner's ONLY effect was to discard a variable bound to the WHOLE empty-list
argument -- exactly the case where the binding IS a fact. It survived because
it was masking fz-kdt.210's defect: delete it before that landed and seven
fixtures produced wrong answers.

WHY THIS TICKET SHRANK: it used to carry an OPENNESS axis (a variable is a
fact only when every positive occurrence contributed). fz-kdt.210 retired
that -- it marks wherever the walk could not read an occurrence AT ALL, which
is the strictly larger set than "the witness carries vars". Both of this
ticket's headline goals then fall out of the deletion alone.

DELETED, 147 lines with zero warnings: drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings
(12), collect_ambiguous_empty_list_vars (72),
collect_ambiguous_tuple_field_vars (52), is_exact_empty_list (7) and the call
site in instantiate_match (1). instantiated_match -> instantiated_clause. Zero
dangling references to any deleted or renamed symbol across src, .agent,
fixtures2, tests and tools.

RED-FIRST: empty_list_binding_is_a_fact spliced onto base production fails
with Underconstrained; it asserts STRUCTURALLY via is_equivalent, not by a
rendered string. On the corpus Kernel.dbg/1[fp[L] empty_list()] and main/0[]
both move from `return fp[any] any` to `return fp[L] empty_list()`.
dead_closure_capture_empty_list CONVERGES: four release binaries (Agenda::pop
pop_front vs pop_back) give base 2 canon movers and head ZERO, at 5755/5755
executables either way -- both schedule-dependent fixtures settle, which is
more than this ticket ever claimed.

MEASURED (605 fixtures from the tree, 476 dumps; both binaries built in this
worktree so fz-kdt.211's embedded path cancels; stdout+stderr normalised for
thread id and hex addresses): interp 0 movers, run 0 movers, and the seven
fixtures that used to regress -- 00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family,
enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs --
are BYTE-IDENTICAL on both doors. Executables 5755 -> 5755. Canon 20 movers,
every one classified: 14 where a published `return fp[any] any` becomes
concrete (12 of them main/0, where an early-revision `[]` had routed dbg's
declared `t: any` into a cumulative return that never retracts; 00032 typed
the returned value list(int) two lines above the `any` it published), 2
activation-key moves, 3 reduce-step key widenings, and 1 SPAN-ONLY
(spec_shared_var_self_composition, whose header this ticket rewrites).

THE ELEVEN RE-PINS, each with its reason, and two of them fix defects rather
than merely move: A8 goes Invalid -> Underconstrained int | [], a FALSE
Invalid removed; X6 goes to Known [int] and now AGREES with its control X6B;
R20 becomes Invalid and is renamed to say why (a >= int against a <= none --
the veto had been removing the lower bound); X4/X4B become Known [] because
the argument supplies exactly [] at that field; X7 is Known [none] with a
structural assert that it instantiates back to [[]]; A3 is Known [] | [int]
with an is_equivalent assert that this is the same SET as [int], the interning
being fz-kdt.182's; and the cleaner's own pin,
the_empty_list_cleaner_decides_which_exception_applies, is flipped
deliberately to an_observed_empty_list_does_not_fall_back_to_a_declared_bound.
The contract_test empty-list witness keeps its result half (None, now for the
right reason) and pins its parameter half KNOWN-WRONG naming fz-kdt.216.

THE MOVEMENTS, JUSTIFIED RATHER THAN RE-BLESSED. Blind-escape census 169 ->
171 plans: a CURE. Both new plans are Region::TupleArity, one apiece on the
two enum_take_drop_split fixtures -- keying on the accumulator the fold really
carries means the body's two rungs must be told apart, so each artifact grows
an entry-clause dispatch, the same statement fz-kdt.183 and fz-kdt.199 made.
(The readable denominator is 7 either way; the column that moved is the
UNREADABLE one.) fz-kdt.63 activation claims 267 -> 271: a COST, and it is
fz-kdt.192's fall being repaid -- 192 booked 259 -> 256 because four tuple
parameters had one field's [] veto the variable for the whole position, and
now that the join absorbs [] those positions publish their narrowed surface
again. Bounded, and not all cost: CallSiteSummary first appearances FALL 473
-> 471 and retractions FALL 18 -> 11, with uncaused 0 and executables flat at
237. A THIRD movement the earlier stacked runs could not see, because their
base predated fz-kdt.187: enum_take_drop_split observations 375 -> 373 at all
six arrivals with escapes FLAT AT 0 -- the denominator moved with the plan
shape, Region::Type questions flat at 62.

GATE: Coordinator gate on the folded commit (marker COORD-GATE-1788484723): fmt clean, zero build warnings, clippy clean, doctests clean, lib 1721 passed / 0 failed / 5 ignored in 80.1 s, fixture matrix single-threaded 515 passed / 0 failed / 3 ignored.

comments.text: fz-kdt.183 landed (2e0bb2706): unblocked. With proto120.diff stacked on this base, enum_map_family, enum_tier0 and fz_f98_map_reduce are byte-equal to expected and dead_closure_capture_empty_list + 00277 are FIFO/LIFO byte-identical. Handoff hazard: proto120.diff also edits .agent/docs/{externs,semantic-fixpoint,specs}.md and fixtures2/behavior/spec_shared_var_self_composition.fz, so `git checkout -- src` does not revert it. Re-cut on fz-kdt.184 (which re-cuts on 192, which waits on 198) before building.

fz-kdt.192 landed (343f3a134): open_vars(params, args) deletes -- instantiate_match already walks (params, args) once, so OpenVars becomes an out-parameter of that walk. This ticket also DELETES the empty-list cleaner, which is the real fix for D3/R20/X6: the per-parameter veto scope is now pinned as a precision loss in two places (r20_cleaner_flip_inside_one_position, x6_one_tuple_parameter_two_fields, against x6b_two_parameters_same_constraint), and 192 widened its corpus exposure from 1 row to 8. Marking ambiguity at the moment of binding removes the scope, the disagreement, and collect_ambiguous_tuple_field_vars with it. Re-cut on 184 (which re-cuts on 192).

fz-kdt.184 landed (ca23b676f): the polarity spine is in place and ready for you to fold onto. arrow_match.rs now has BindingSide { Unify, Lower, Upper } with a total flipped(), MatchBounds { lower, upper } threaded through all six collectors, and collect_arrow_match as the one reversing node. 120 re-cuts to: replace OpenVars.positive with BindingSide (it IS the polarity, measured), add OpenVars.vars (openness, the distinct axis this ticket did NOT add), and DELETE drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings -- which 184 deliberately left polarity-blind and inert at arrow_match.rs:585 exactly so you delete it whole. The empty-list ambiguity drop, dbg([]) = [], and dead_closure_capture_empty_list convergence are yours. Re-cut on this base (343f3a134 + 184); the old proto120.diff predates 192 and 184 and will not apply.

STACKED MEASUREMENT handed over from fz-kdt.210 (commit 89022c7cf on
wt/kdt210-build, base dd07432db). Measured by the 210 builder, not relayed.

The experiment: 210 as landed, plus a ~147-line deletion of
`drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings`, `collect_ambiguous_empty_list_vars`,
`collect_ambiguous_tuple_field_vars`, `is_exact_empty_list` and the single call
site in `instantiate_match`. NOTHING ELSE -- no openness axis, no
`MatchBounds.vars`. Zero build warnings. The experiment was reverted; 210 is
one commit and contains none of it.

Result vs base dd07432db, 605 fixtures:

  interp stdout+stderr (normalised)   2 movers -- the two fixtures 210 revives
  run    stdout+stderr (normalised)   2 movers -- the same two
  the seven fixtures 120 could not move (00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family,
    enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges,
    mailbox_closure_enum_hofs)       BYTE-IDENTICAL to base on interp AND run
  canon md5 movers                    23   (120's own scope)
  executables                         5755 -- identical to 210 alone
  FIFO/LIFO canon movers, whole tree  base 2, 210 alone 2, STACKED 0
    (`dead_closure_capture_empty_list` and
     `with_index_users_keep_nested_list_elements` both converge, 5755/5755)
  `dbg([])` published return          base and 210 `fp[any] any`;
                                      stacked `fp[L] empty_list()`
  `Enum.reverse/1([int])`             `list(int)`

So both of 120's headline goals fall out of the DELETION alone. 120's openness
axis is subsumed for the RESULT half -- 210 marks wherever the walk could not
read an occurrence at all, the strictly larger set. Re-cut 120 as a deletion
and re-measure rather than carrying the axis forward.

`cargo test --lib` on the stacked tree: 1707 passed / 12 failed / 5 ignored
(debug; the release-only `metadata_macro_rejects_duplicate_keys` is red at base
too and is not in this count). Eleven are calculator re-pins 120 owns:

  tests::empty_list_binding_is_ambiguous
  contract_test::function_contract_application_treats_empty_list_witness_as_underconstrained
  pinned_verdicts::x4_mixed_arity_tuple_union_drops_the_empty_list_binding
  pinned_verdicts::x4b_same_arity_tuple_union_drops_the_empty_list_binding
  pinned_verdicts::x6_one_tuple_parameter_two_fields
  pinned_verdicts::x7_empty_list_one_level_down
  pinned_verdicts::a3_reducer_parameter_widening
  pinned_verdicts::a8_three_positions_one_variable
  pinned_verdicts::r20_cleaner_flip_inside_one_position
  pinned_verdicts::the_empty_list_cleaner_decides_which_exception_applies  <-- NEW at 210
  (the last one is 210's own seam pin: with the cleaner intact an `[]`-only
   binding is dropped from Sigma and routes into the "observed nowhere"
   exception, so the verdict is Known; deleting the cleaner leaves it in Sigma,
   it is marked, and the verdict becomes Underconstrained. 120 must flip it
   deliberately.)

The remaining two are MOVEMENTS, not re-pins, and 120's gate must justify them:

  drive_test::compiler2_dispatch_blind_escape_census_is_the_known_population
    entry plans 169 -> 171, readable 162 -> 164
  public_trace_test::analysis_claims_survive_a_run_that_could_not_re_derive_them
    fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz activation claims 267 -> 271
    (+4), an fz-kdt.63 COST pin. Behaviour is unmoved and its executable count
    is unchanged at 237, but compile work rises on the arc's slowest fixture.

None of 120's 13 blocking drive_test/JIT regressions appear.

fz-kdt.210 landed (5a1ba823b) and YOU ARE NOW A PURE DELETION. Measured by stacking your cleaner removal on top of 210 and then reverting: interp and run each move only the two fixtures 210 revives; the seven fixtures that previously regressed (00276, 00277, 00420, enum_map_family, enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, mailbox_closure_enum_hofs) are BYTE-IDENTICAL to base on both doors; executables stay at 5,755 (identical to 210 alone); dbg([]) publishes empty_list() instead of any; Enum.reverse/1([int]) types as list(int); and FIFO/LIFO canon movers go to ZERO at 5,755/5,755 -- both schedule-dependent fixtures converge, which is better than your ticket ever claimed.

YOUR OPENNESS AXIS IS RETIRED: 210 marks wherever the walk could not read an occurrence at all, which is the strictly larger set than "the witness carries vars". Both of your headline goals now fall out of the cleaner deletion alone. So re-cut to: delete drop_ambiguous_empty_list_bindings and its three helpers (147 lines, 0 warnings), rename instantiated_match -> instantiated_clause, fix the fz-f98.16 doc sentences, and re-pin.

WHAT YOUR GATE MUST JUSTIFY, measured on the stacked tree (lib 1707/12): eleven calculator re-pins you own -- the reviewer's ten plus the_empty_list_cleaner_decides_which_exception_applies, which you must flip deliberately -- and TWO movements that are not re-pins: blind-escape entry plans 169 -> 171 (readable 162 -> 164) and enum_take_drop_split activation claims 267 -> 271, the latter an fz-kdt.63 COST ratchet. Neither is a correctness regression, but your gate must state why each is right rather than re-blessing it.

title: A @spec variable is a lower bound and a fact only when every positive occurrence contributed: the empty-list ambiguity drop goes, dbg([]) is [], and dead_closure_capture_empty_list converges
